title: Regularity agrees at common maximum-history stages
statement: Let $V$ be totally ordered with least element, let $\nu$ be a supplied resolution invariant calculus [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data], and let $A$ be an embedded rational pair [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. Let $T$ and $U$ be chronological maximum segments [lem-trf-maximum-history-chronology] of lengths $r$ and $s$ over $A$; their prefixes are admissible, their extensions are maximum steps and all sources of extensions are nonregular [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. For every natural number $i\leq r,s$, the final scheme of the length-$i$ prefix in $T$ is regular if and only if that in $U$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. No regularity of the two terminal stages and no labeled lower-cut realization are assumed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.1.1--2.1.4, 2.3.4 and 2.3.11, printed pp.86--87,91--93; common-prefix canonical comparison induction from original finite-realization Step 3

proof.text: Induct on the common prefix, identifying initial ambient and intrinsic diagrams through their normalized isomorphisms with A. Maintain commuting ambient and intrinsic isomorphisms on the entire prefix, preserving earlier ideals. They give a smooth history comparison over the identity initial pair, with identity index map and no deletions.

SmoothValues identifies the invariant functions under that comparison. Their greatest positive values and full loci agree. The new centers are reduced, hence on each affine open they have the same radical ideal cutting out that locus. Their intrinsic ideals, and then their ambient ideals through the compatible closed immersions, agree. Principalization makes the common extended ideal invertible on both blowups. The blowup universal property lifts the preceding isomorphism in both directions, and uniqueness makes the lifts inverse.

The ambient comparison takes the same open complement and its scheme-theoretic closure to one another, so it identifies strict transforms and extends the induction. At the desired common stage, isomorphisms preserve local Noetherianity and identify stalk rings, so regularity agrees. The induction uses only the indicated prefix, not terminal regularity or tower padding.

theorem maximumHistorySegment_commonStage {V : Type w} [LinearOrder V] [OrderBot V]
    {ν : ResolutionInvariantCalculus.{u} V} {A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {r s : ℕ}
    (T : MaximumHistorySegment ν A r) (U : MaximumHistorySegment ν A s)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ r) (hj : i ≤ s) :
    IsRegularScheme (T.history ⟨i, Nat.lt_succ_of_le hi⟩).X ↔
      IsRegularScheme (U.history ⟨i, Nat.lt_succ_of_le hj⟩).X
